tasks.short: Evaluate staff leading exercise or diagnostic tests

steps.what: Observe staff leading group exercise or conducting diagnostic tests against role expectations
Evaluate performance findings and discuss the assessment with the staff member

tasks.design: Keep observation and staff assessment with the exercise physiologist. Existing role expectations in {DOCS} can support discussion without automated performance scoring.
tasks.previous_blocker: Performance assessment depends on observed practice, context and staff explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference tools can display expectations but do not replace competent observation.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing individual performance from circumstances requires judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The evaluator considers context and gives constructive feedback.
tasks.altitude: Assessment time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Give feedback on supervised exercise practice
reach.learn: Specific behavioral feedback and clinical context

evidence.claim: Staff assessment remains contextual human judgement; this unchanged design introduces no automated scoring or measured saving.

assumptions: Boundary is the exercise physiologist's observation and assessment, excluding staff participation time and subsequent employment decisions.
The exercise physiologist produces observed performance findings in s1. Staff explanation is heard during s2 before the assessment is finalized; no structured competency flag is assumed.
Use existing native document access before new tools. No recording, employee monitoring model or automated ranking is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because the evaluation process is unchanged.
research_questions: Is any repeated assessment paperwork distinct from observation and feedback?

approvals.approved_version: Exact observed findings, contextual explanation and assessment discussed in s2; changes require renewed consideration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Strong performance and disputed observations both retain contextual evaluation and discussion.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Mentor or train staff through demonstration, supervised practice and feedback on group exercise

tasks.design: Keep demonstrations, supervised practice and mentoring with the exercise physiologist. Existing learning references in {LMS} can support practice without replacing individual feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mentoring requires observing how staff actually lead a group.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning resources support reference use but do not establish equivalent practical coaching.
tasks.still_hard: Responding to unexpected participant needs requires live judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The mentor identifies specific improvements and adapts coaching to the learner.
tasks.altitude: Practical training time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coach safe and effective exercise instruction

evidence.claim: Practical mentoring combines demonstration and individual feedback; no task replacement is established here.

assumptions: Boundary covers practical mentoring, excluding separate course material creation and formal performance evaluation.
The mentor observes practice during s1; no pre-existing structured competence score is assumed.
Check native learning references before custom tools. Existing learning content maintenance remains unchanged.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new training software or capture process is introduced. Resolve overlap with performance evaluation once in roll-ups.
unknowns: Staff experience and practical training format
research_questions: Which learning needs require live observation rather than self-study references?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. New instructors and experienced staff learning new activities retain practical feedback.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present exercise knowledge and research findings

steps.what: Select exercise knowledge, program information and research findings for the professional audience
Draft presentation explanations and speaker notes from the selected findings

loop.purpose: Draft concise explanations of selected program and research material
loop.input: presentation brief with source passages and checked results
loop.check: Physiologist checks numerical interpretation, limitations, clinical meaning and suitability for the audience
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported or misleading explanations are rewritten manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates handle layout but not contextual explanation of research findings

steps.what: Check the presentation and present findings while answering professional audience questions

tasks.design: Use native presentation templates in {DOCS} and a bounded drafting loop for source-grounded explanations. The physiologist checks the exact presentation and delivers it, including discussion, personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected findings still needed repeated prose and speaker-note composition.
tasks.enabler_now: Writing assistance can propose editable explanations from a supplied brief.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical implications, study limitations and live questions require expertise.
tasks.human_edge: The physiologist explains uncertainty and corrects misleading interpretations.
tasks.altitude: A small preparation saving leaves professional communication and responsibility unchanged.

reach.task: Explain research implications for exercise practice

evidence.claim: Drafting explanatory presentation prose from selected findings is plausible assistance; this design and its labour estimate are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary includes presentation preparation and delivery, excluding conducting research and collecting program data.

The exercise physiologist produces in s1 audience, duration, selected findings, checked figures and units, source passages, limitations and intended messages. Selection, capture and interpretation remain counted; missing support requires manual wording.
Test native templates and reuse of approved presentation material before the drafting loop. Only permitted source material enters the tool, without patient-identifiable data.
Research production and data checks retain their existing owners and are not claimed as savings. Live delivery and final checks retain all s3 time.
unknowns: Existing presentation reuse and source access
research_questions: Does checked drafting reduce preparation after correction of research interpretations?

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and source checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact presentation text, figures, references and speaker notes checked before delivery in s3; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R92.5 gross7.5 minus4 upkeep gives net3.5. Range0-1 assumes substantial existing slide reuse and intensive interpretation checks; delivery and discussion retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess clinical context and determine whether diagnostic procedures should be recommended
Check the patient and intended procedure before issuing an authorized order or recommendation

tasks.design: Keep procedure selection and release with the authorized professional. Native order entry in the clinical record {OTHER} supports the action without inferring the clinical indication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selecting a diagnostic procedure depends on clinical context and professional scope.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order tools support entry but do not replace clinical judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Indications, patient circumstances and scope boundaries require professional assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The physiologist recognizes when another authorized clinician must decide or order.
tasks.altitude: Clinical judgement and ordering rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify the clinical question for diagnostic testing
reach.learn: Appropriate referral communication and scope boundaries

evidence.claim: Diagnostic procedure judgement and authorized release remain human work; existing order entry establishes no additional saving.

assumptions: Boundary is the physiologist's recommendation or order within verified local scope, excluding performing tests and a separate clinician's authorization. No new ordering right is assumed.

The exercise physiologist produces procedure judgement in s1 and checks patient identity, intended procedure and authority in s2. No structured eligible-for-test or approved-indication flag is assumed.
OTHER denotes the clinical record and order system. Test native functions before custom tools; existing automatic field population is not human baseline.
Zero incremental upkeep because no decision support or ordering automation is introduced.
unknowns: Professional scope and local ordering procedures
research_questions: Is there measurable duplicate entry after the clinical decision that is distinct from authorized release?

already_counted.description: Patient, procedure and authority check before release

incremental.description: No new diagnostic ordering automation upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, procedure, clinical question and order or recommendation checked before release in s2; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Straightforward recommendations and uncertain clinical indications retain judgement and authorized release.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Presentation drafting may shrink while staff evaluation, mentoring and clinical procedure judgement remain with the physiologist.
reach: Learn practical feedback approaches from physical therapists
Clarify diagnostic questions with referring physicians
role.ambitious_version: An exercise physiologist with modest presentation support and unchanged responsibility for people and clinical judgement.
